items.summary: Jensen Huang stepped down as Nvidia chief executive following reports of three affairs, leaving the company without a permanent successor and no succession plan. Prediction market Kalshi showed odds for naming Huang next permanent CEO rose to 15% before falling to around 7%, while Ian Buck leads at 33%. Colette Kress sits at 13%. Tech figures including Elon Musk and Donald Trump voiced support, with Trump suggesting Tim Cook as successor; Polymarket implied a 6% chance for Cook. Nvidia shares rebounded from US$150 to around US$162 after the ousting.
items.title: Prediction Markets Bet on Jensen Huang's Return as Nvidia CEO Amid Succession Uncertainty

items.summary: NVIDIA's cuBLAS, in CUDA Toolkit 13.4.2, accelerates full double-precision (FP64) dense matrix multiplications by breaking numbers into integer pieces and multiplying them exactly on GPU Tensor Cores via the Automatic Dynamic Precision framework. Two new algorithms—Ozaki-II, which needs roughly half the GEMMs of Ozaki-I at FP64 accuracy, and a 2M complex-multiply method—are chosen automatically with no code changes. DGEMM runs up to 5.5x faster on VR NVL72 and 3.9x on GB200; CCSD quantum-chemistry workloads reach 11.5x over native FP64, while BerkeleyGW materials simulations gain 6.6x.
items.title: NVIDIA cuBLAS FP64 Emulation Speeds Double-Precision Matrix Math on Tensor Cores

items.summary: An extramarital affair has renewed global scrutiny on chip giant Nvidia and its Singapore-based client Megaspeed, which is suspected of helping China access advanced US semiconductors barred from export. Observers told CNA that the saga could soon make things trickier for Singapore in the semiconductor space. Matthias Hendrichs noted Singapore's deep ties with both Washington and Beijing mean it has less room to manoeuvre on this technology. Associate Professor Chong Ja Ian warned of a 'Singapore washing' perception, though Singapore does not implement unilateral foreign export controls. Analysts expect more US pressure, tighter rules for Southeast Asia, higher compliance costs and slower transactions, affecting the trading side rather than manufacturing.
items.title: Nvidia-Megaspeed Saga Could Squeeze Singapore's Room in Chips Space, Slow Things for Firms: Analysts

items.summary: The S&P 500 fell 31.53 points (0.42%) to 7,560.87 while the Nasdaq dropped 230.13 points (0.91%), but the Dow rose 46.14 points (0.09%). Nvidia's sixth straight weekly decline followed CEO Jensen Huang's resignation amid personal-conduct revelations; Arm Holdings' Rene Haas is a potential successor, raising AI-trade concerns. Weak October producer prices still supported at least a 25-basis-point December Fed hike.
items.title: US Stocks Close Lower on Nvidia Leadership Uncertainty and Rate-Hike Bets

items.summary: A global outage of Microsoft's Outlook and Teams eased after more than 24 hours, though the company gave no timeline for full recovery. Server issues caused the incident, which also affected its Copilot AI assistant; Microsoft ruled out malicious activity and AI as causes. A broader rollout of software fixes was stabilizing systems. The two workplace applications serve hundreds of millions of users worldwide.
items.title: Microsoft Outlook and Teams Outage Eases After More Than a Day

items.summary: On Friday (local time), Microsoft apologized to customers and partners after a global outage disrupted services including Outlook email, Microsoft Teams and Copilot. The company attributed the incident to a technical issue linked to an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change, explicitly ruling out any cyberattack or AI-agent involvement. The disruption affected at least 74 countries, including the United States, leaving millions of users without access for nearly 18 hours and impacting airline operations worldwide, prompting major Indian carriers to issue passenger advisories.
items.title: Microsoft Apologizes After Global Outage Disrupts Outlook, Teams and Copilot for Nearly 18 Hours

items.summary: Nvidia founder Jensen Huang stepped down after admitting an affair with Alice Huang, who ran Megaspeed, a major Nvidia chip buyer. The case has spotlighted tensions in Singapore's role as a global semiconductor hub. Last year it was Nvidia's second-largest market globally, yet less than 1% of its earnings came from chips physically present there, since the island routes orders onward to Asia. Since US export restrictions on advanced chips reached China in 2022, officials worry countries like Singapore could be used for illicit access; Megaspeed is suspected of giving Chinese firms backdoor chip access via data centres in Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand. Singapore has charged four companies and five individuals but brought no charges against Megaspeed-linked parties after finding insufficient evidence against Alice Huang.
items.title: How the Jensen Huang scandal created a headache for business-friendly Singapore

items.summary: On Friday, a regulatory filing revealed that Soros Fund Management significantly increased its third-quarter stake in Intel, building a 2.83 million-share position valued at $340.3 million from just 100,000 shares held by end of June.
items.title: Soros Fund Management Ramps Up Intel Stake in Q3

items.summary: A global Microsoft outage struck the UK on Friday, causing serious and widespread disruption across healthcare, courts, police and property services. The NHS reported hundreds of hospitals, GP surgeries and community health services affected as staff lost access to email, meetings and patient data; some fell back on paper records while operations were cancelled or delayed. Courts saw cases at magistrates', crown and civil levels — including in Manchester and Scotland — postponed after the judiciary's reliance on Microsoft platforms. Police online reporting was down but 999 remained unaffected, with staff returning to phone contact. Property agents relied on direct communication as end-of-week moves continued.
items.title: Microsoft Outage Disrupts Key UK Public Services

items.summary: Despite co-founding and leading Nvidia for 33 years, Jensen Huang's roughly 870 million shares—about 3.6% of the company—did not grant him absolute control. Nearly 800 million were held via trusts shared with his wife; about 70 million directly. His November 12 resignation underscores that large ownership does not guarantee board authority.
items.title: Jensen Huang's Nvidia Shareholding Fell Short of Board Control

items.summary: Four federal agencies—the Federal Reserve Board, FDIC, NCUA, and OCC—announced on November 13, 2026, that they will extend the comment period for proposed third-party risk management guidance until December 16. Originally due November 16, comments now target supervisory experience-based principles designed to help banks and credit unions tailor practices to individual relationships. The non-binding guidance is intended to be rescinded upon finalization.
items.title: Federal Agencies Extend Comment Period for Third-Party Risk Management Guidance

items.summary: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO amid reports of relationships with two employees, including Alice Huang, suspected by US intelligence of working for Beijing; a third woman was also linked to him. Separately, Microsoft suffered one of its worst outages after taking over as the world's most valuable company, lasting at least 18 hours due to server overload and unexpected unavailability.
items.title: Microsoft Outage and Nvidia Leadership Fallout

items.summary: Jensen Huang's sudden resignation has raised questions about who will lead the world's most prominent AI chip company, with interim CFO Collete Kriss named. Among seven candidates discussed are Ian Buck, Lisa Su of AMD, Rene Haas of Arm, John Srouji of Apple, and former Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger.
items.title: Seven Candidates Emerge for Nvidia CEO Role After Jensen Huang's Resignation

items.summary: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's CEO after reports of two extramarital affairs, including one with Alice Huang (Huang Le), a suspected Chinese spy. Sen. Tim Scott requested that Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick testify before the Senate Banking Committee, warning he could be subpoenaed if he declines. Huang was also summoned by House committees for a December 1 interview.
items.title: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Summoned by Congress Over Spy Scandal

items.summary: A failure in Microsoft's server infrastructure has cut users off from Outlook email, Teams and Copilot for more than a day, with problems reported across 74 countries. The disruption began Thursday afternoon European time and was still not fully fixed Friday morning; by then Microsoft reported only marginal success after overnight fixes crashed again under returning traffic. No cyber attack is indicated, though speculation persists amid no confirmed cause or timeline. Beyond missed emails, the outage affected UK GP practices, Singapore's government, Australian intelligence services, OpenAI and Anthropic, and Workhorse postponed an earnings call. Experts warn of Europe's heavy reliance on a handful of US tech giants.
items.title: Microsoft outage explained: what went wrong and is your data at risk?

items.summary: Google and Samsung announced preorders for a line of smart glasses, released in partnership with eyewear brands Gentle Monster (six styles) and Warby Parker (three models), challenging category leader Meta. The nine styles ship around Dec. 10 at $449 or $395, weigh about 41 grams, offer up to nine hours of battery life, and include a charging case with seven top-ups. They run on Android XR, feature HDR cameras, binaural audio, navigation, translation, and Gemini AI integration, compatible with iPhones and select Google/Samsung devices. Emphasizing privacy amid Meta’s pushback—nicknamed “pervert glasses”—Google will disable recording if the indicator light is tampered with, redact bystander faces before processing, require user consent agreements, and restrict apps from live-streaming or facial identification.
items.title: Google and Samsung Set to Release AI Smart Glasses in December

items.summary: IndiGo, India's largest airline, said Friday its email support was disrupted by a global Microsoft service outage beginning late Thursday night. The carrier rerouted emails to maintain uninterrupted communication and continued responding within its usual 24-hour timeline, while confirming all other channels remain available and flight operations unaffected. Microsoft attributed the strain—not increased traffic—to servers unexpectedly becoming unavailable, with no evidence of malicious activity as of an 11:16 am IST service-health update.
items.title: Microsoft Outage Impacts IndiGo's Email Support Services

items.summary: The Atlantic States Marine Fisheries Commission’s Menhaden Management Board cut coastwide catch limits by about 9 percent in both 2027 and 2028, reducing the total allowable catch from 170,000 metric tons to 155,000 metric tons. The Chesapeake Bay cap fell further—by 27 percent then 34 percent—and tied reduction fishing to 21.8 percent of the coastwide limit. Conservationists welcomed the cuts but warned they fall short: a deeper cut would only yield a 50 percent chance of meeting an ecological target that excludes ospreys, whose Bay nesting success dropped sharply. The industry pushed back, citing economic harm and calling for research before further restrictions.
items.title: ASMFC Lowers Menhaden Caps Despite Conservationist Concerns

items.summary: The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop on Friday, delaying or canceling more than 11,000 flights across the US and plunging airports into chaos. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy attributed it to “a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers,” while DHS Director Markwayne Mullin said preliminary investigations showed no indication of a nefarious attack, calling it instead a telecommunications outage. Officials prioritized landing airborne aircraft but offered no timeline for resuming departures. CNN reported the FAA blamed router malfunctions originating at Chicago Midway airport that rippled nationwide. This was the third such grounding in US history, following 9/11 and January 2023.
items.title: FAA Nationwide Ground Stop Disrupts US Airports

items.summary: Jojo, an 11-year-old male gorilla rescued as an infant from Gabon's private zoo where his family was killed by poachers, has spent nearly his entire life alone. His carers at the Lekedi Foundation want to find him a companion, possibly another rescued or zoo-bred gorilla. Researchers including Prof Gillian Forrester of Sussex and Dr Robin Morrison of Zurich note that being bonded with others is vital for great ape psychology; Morrison's study found female mountain gorillas seek familiar companions when joining groups. However, no suitable match has emerged despite contacts with accredited zoos, as international translocation rules are built for breeding programmes rather than companion introductions or wild reintroductions.
items.title: Jojo the gorilla seeks a companion after decades of solitary confinement

items.summary: On Nov 13, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed lower as concerns over Nvidia pressured technology shares. Nvidia's stock fell 2% for its sixth straight week after CEO Jensen Huang resigned amid revelations of extramarital affairs. The Dow rose modestly to 52,347.55 while the S&P 500 lost 30.73 points and the Nasdaq dropped 229.82 points. For the week, however, all three indexes posted gains as Nvidia's decline snapped a four-week losing streak for the S&P 500 and Nasdaq. Separately, October producer prices rose 6.5% year over year, keeping expectations for a December rate hike intact.
items.title: US Tech Shares and Inflation Data Weigh on Markets Amid Nvidia Leadership Uncertainty

items.summary: On Friday, US stock indexes fell amid renewed concerns about Nvidia after CEO Jensen Huang's resignation reignited a technology selloff. The Philadelphia semiconductor index dropped 6%, with Advanced Micro Devices and Broadcom falling 10% and 7%. Soft October producer prices data offered little relief as inflation remained elevated at 6.5% year over year, prompting warnings that the AI trade faces fresh headwinds.
items.title: US Stocks Tumble as Nvidia Slides 4.3%, Triggering Fresh Selloff in Technology Shares

items.summary: Per the Financial Times, Nvidia's board approached British chipmaker Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas in its search for a successor to Jensen Huang. Reports indicate some employees are pushing to bring back the former chief executive, who stepped down Thursday amid revelations of extramarital affairs and allegations involving a suspected Chinese spy. Analysts had already floated Haas' name; he spent seven years at Nvidia before joining Arm in 2013.
items.title: Nvidia Approaches Arm CEO Haas as Employees Seek Huang's Return

items.summary: Institutional investor interest in Anthropic's initial public offering is outpacing SpaceX's earlier roadshow, with demand growing from roughly two times oversubscribed on day one to six times by Thursday. Bankers attribute the strength to the deal's size and expect continued growth as investors weigh whether Anthropic can sustain its AI lead amid rapid competition from Alphabet's Google. Valuation hinges on projected 2028 revenue of $270 billion to $280 billion, though sell-side estimates for 2026 range from $52 billion to $53 billion and buy-side projections vary further, with some running up to 10% to 15% higher while others sit about 30% below. Limited disclosure during the roadshow has left key questions unanswered.
items.title: Investor Demand and Valuation Uncertainty Surround Anthropic's $64 Billion IPO

items.summary: This item is a single-panel political cartoon by Martin Rowson satirizing Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang, framed around his 'downfall.' The piece offers no accompanying article text, figures, or further context beyond its captioned title. It functions purely as visual commentary rather than reporting on specific events or claims about the company's performance.
items.title: Martin Rowson on the downfall of Nvidia's Jensen Huang – cartoon

items.summary: Nvidia co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang stepped down after 33 years, sending shockwaves through the startup ecosystem. Investors say his departure removes a dominant champion that backed nearly every AI-native company from application to neocloud, injecting tens of billions annually across 105 rounds this year alone as its largest investor in many deals. His conservative successor Colette Kress is expected to write smaller checks and be more selective, threatening valuations and early-stage funding—especially outside the U.S., where Nvidia's support created a gap no one can fill.
items.title: Jensen Huang's Departure Blasts Big Hole in AI Startup Funding

items.summary: The FTC plans to file suit today to block a $3.5 billion merger of CD&R and TPG-owned Covetrus from acquiring MWI Veterinary Supply, citing increased costs for pet owners and clinics. Officials say the deal would create a highly concentrated market; neither company commented. The move reflects leadership under Andrew Ferguson's focus on affordability in President Trump's agenda.
items.title: FTC Plans to Block $3.5 Billion Veterinary Merger

items.summary: Anthropic's IPO is reportedly six times oversubscribed, signaling investor optimism in the AI sector despite recent tech weakness and a Nasdaq monthly loss its largest in over a year. Nvidia's CEO resignation intensified concerns about spending and debt. Yet some investors remain confident: Goldman Sachs, an underwriter, projects Anthropic's revenue surpassing $600 billion by 2030—more than 130 times last year's sales.
items.title: Demand Remains Strong for Anthropic IPO Despite Tech Pullback

items.summary: Eighteen patent applications filed in India for lenacapavir, a breakthrough HIV therapy, have raised concerns they could prolong market exclusivity and delay affordable generics. Patient groups and civil society contest the move with regulatory authorities, arguing the applications lack novelty and inventive steps. The filings exemplify 'evergreening,' where secondary patents on minor variations extend exclusivity to keep prices high and restrict patient access.
items.title: Breakthrough HIV Drug Sees 18 Patent Filings in India, May Delay Affordable Generics

items.summary: The Leh Apex Body's indefinite dharna entered its second day amid intensifying protests against the government's decision to hold Ladakh hill council elections on Dec 4, despite opposition from the LAB and Kargil Democratic Alliance. Religious heads would lead a hunger strike from Saturday at NDS memorial park in Leh. Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk said he was forcibly confined; police denied him leaving his residence after preventive restrictions were imposed for 60 days by the Leh DM.
items.title: Leh Protest Intensifies as Wangchuk Under House Detention

items.summary: The US Federal Aviation Administration issued a rare nationwide ground stop, halting departures and delays to landings at all airports in the United States. The halt began around 4pm ET on Friday and was caused by what officials described as 'a temporary telecommunications outage.' In its statement, the FAA noted that every flight had been accounted for and that international flights would be handled on a case-by-case basis.
items.title: Rare Nationwide FAA Ground Stop Caused by Telecommunications Outage

items.summary: A quality-control failure forced California regulators to discard nearly nine months of air-monitoring data for the fumigants 1,3-D and methyl bromide. Advocates argue this undermines confidence in new rules limiting worker exposure, which they say are weaker than scientific safety targets—allowing residents up to 14 times higher levels while workers face five times higher ones. Reform groups worry emissions rose after a 2024 residential rule took effect, but DPR plans to replace lost data with unverified models that may underestimate risk.
items.title: California's New Pesticide Regulation May Not Protect Workers Amid Lost Air-Monitoring Data

items.summary: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO amid mounting speculation about an alleged espionage plot involving his wife, Alice Huang — a former Megaspeed executive suspected by US intelligence of being a Chinese spy — and two other extra-marital affairs. Congressional Republicans and three House committee chairs are demanding testimony or closed-door interviews from Huang, Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, and Under-Secretary Jeffrey Kessler over AI chip exports to China and stalled trade blacklists. Trump defended Huang despite reports he was briefed on the espionage findings a year ago without acting. Nvidia launched an independent investigation while Colette Kress became interim CEO; it found no evidence of compromised national security or company secrets. Alice Huang, banned from Singapore, reportedly lives in Beijing.
items.title: Questions Left to Answer in Wake of Jensen Huang's Departure

items.summary: At the inaugural African-hosted 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Senegal, Australia won six medals—four silvers and two bronzes. Nearly 2,700 athletes aged 14 to 17 competed across 25 sports over two weeks. Boxer Marley Dodd took silver at 55kg; Mackenzie Macdonald earned Australia's first-ever taekwondo medal in the 49kg category; cyclists Elsie Apps and Caleb McKenzie won silver and bronze respectively, with McKenzie recovering from Hashimoto's disease to claim a late sprint victory. Queensland beach volleyball pair Thomas Turner and Ryan Edgar took bronze. IOC President Kirsty Coventry praised the event as exceeding expectations but cautioned that only about 15% of Youth Olympic athletes progress to the full Olympics. China led medal counts with 18 golds, ahead of Japan (11) and Russia (8). The Games marked a milestone for emerging Australian talent heading toward Brisbane 2032.
items.title: Australia's Youth Olympic Medal Haul as Dakar Games Celebrated

items.summary: The South African Supreme Court of Appeal dismissed the government's appeal in the #CancelCoal case, upholding a High Court ruling that struck down plans for 1,500 megawatts of new coal-fired power. Environmental NGOs argued it violated children's constitutional right to a healthy environment, citing over 2,200 annual deaths from air pollution. The Minister can still appeal to the Constitutional Court.
items.title: South African Court Dismisses Appeal Over Planned Coal-Fired Power Plants

items.summary: India's apex drug regulator, the Drugs Controller General of India (DCGI) Rajeev Singh Raghuvanshi, ordered an immediate halt to manufacturing, sale, and distribution of obeticholic acid tablets and directed companies to recall the chronic liver disease medication pending a fresh safety review. The DCGI sought cancellation of licenses for 5mg and 10mg tablets approved in March 2020 to treat primary biliary cholangitis (PBC), following recommendations from CDSCO's expert panel on gastroenterology and hepatology. Global regulators, including the USFDA and European Medicines Agency, recommended revocation due to risks of serious liver injury and lack of confirmed clinical efficacy.
items.title: India Halts Obeticholic Acid Production and Orders Recall Pending Safety Review

items.summary: On November 13th, 2026, the author released datasette-cluster-map version 0.19, one of their oldest and favorite Datasette plugins. It now works with Datasette 1.0a42 and depends on the new datasette-leaflet to request OpenStreetMap tiles with a referrer header. The release includes a map of power plants owned by California's PG&E, demonstrating Datasette's recently redesigned facets.
items.title: datasette-cluster-map 0.19

items.summary: Dayana Blanco Quiroga, an Aymara Indigenous woman from Bolivia's west, co-founded the Uru Uru Team in 2019 to clean the toxic, nearly drained 83-square-mile Uru Uru Lake by hand. The documentary How to Plant a Lake follows her eight-step effort: digging marsh totora plants and transplanting them into polluted water where they absorb heavy metals while being cordoned off from animals. Beyond mining waste dumped near Oruro since the 1990s, drought tied to El Niño and climate change nearly emptied the lake a decade ago. Blanco hopes future generations can say 'we fought for our lake.'
items.title: How a Bolivian Woman Is Reviving a Dying Lake with Plants

items.summary: Sen. Bernie Sanders frames the Democratic Senate leadership contest between Chuck Schumer and Chris Van Hollen not as a personality fight but as a defining debate over the party's future direction. The race, he argues, determines whether Democrats preserve an establishment model reliant on billionaire donors, consultants and TV ads or transform into a grassroots movement for working families.
items.title: What the Schumer–Van Hollen Senate Leadership Race Is Really About

items.summary: Datasette table pages previously sent a Referrer-Policy: no-referrer header, which caused plugins loading tiles from OpenStreetMap to violate that policy. The datasette-leaflet plugin now sets the referrer policy on tile requests themselves to strict-origin-when-cross-origin, passing only the host rather than the full page path. This change lets other Datasette plugins depend on the bundled Leaflet while respecting OSM's hosted tile server requirements.
items.title: datasette-leaflet 0.3 fixes OpenStreetMap referrer policy on tile requests

items.summary: Rinnai launched the REHPW series of electric heat pump water heaters, adding Wi-Fi controls to an appliance that uses less electricity than conventional resistance models. Available in 50-, 65- and 80-gallon sizes with UEF ratings up to 4.0, the units deliver up to 91 gallons per hour and offer top-and-side plumbing connections for simpler installation.
items.title: Rinnai REHPW Heat Pump Water Heaters Add Wi-Fi and Easier Installation

items.summary: US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin are expected to hold an unprecedented trilateral meeting on the sidelines of next week's APEC summit in Shenzhen. Discussions could cover nuclear stockpiles and the war with Iran, though not Ukraine. The three leaders lead the world's largest nuclear powers amid heightened tensions.
items.title: Trump, Xi and Putin Set for Unprecedented Trilateral Meeting in China

items.summary: A freighter named Atlantic Asphalt struck the docked cruise ship The American Heritage near New Orleans' port Friday, causing it to capsize. Over 30 people were hospitalized—none critically—but no deaths occurred; at least 180 passengers and crew were rescued. Mayor Helena Moreno called it "a miracle on the Mississippi." The vessel, operated by American Cruise Lines, was mid-eight-day cruise.
items.title: Tanker Collides with Cruise Ship on Mississippi in New Orleans

items.summary: The FAA is expanding its $875 million SMART system, an AI tool advising controllers on scheduling and routing, from the National Capital Region to all 22 national airspace centers. Since launching over Washington, DC airspace in September, it rerouted 180 flights, saving about 10 minutes and nearly 80 gallons of fuel per flight. Airlines support the rollout; the controller union says it was not involved. Human specialists still validate recommendations before use.
items.title: FAA Expands AI Air-Traffic Tool Nationwide After DC Success

items.summary: European Council President Antonio Costa announced that the EU would send a diplomatic team, not a single envoy, to upcoming Ukraine talks alongside five Coalition of the Willing nations: the UK, France, Germany, Italy and Poland. The move addresses fears that US-led negotiations could sideline Europe while Moscow and Washington shape the conflict's outcome. Leaders remain divided over representation—Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov demanded one European voice, but a team was chosen instead to include coalition members like the UK. Optimism is tempered by pessimism: Donald Tusk dismissed talks as exaggerated, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz warned of an 'Anchorage moment,' and Andris Kulbergs stressed Europe's collective strength.
items.title: EU Sends Five-Power Diplomatic Team for Ukraine Talks Amid Disputes Over Representation and Timing

items.summary: India's merchandise exports reached a record $49.47 billion in October 2026, up 45% year-on-year and the fastest monthly growth in five years, per commerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal. Petroleum products drove export gains (+140%), while imports rose 16.51% to $89.35 billion as West Asian conflict pushed crude near $120 a barrel; India sources over 85% of its crude abroad. The trade deficit narrowed to $39.88 billion, and combined goods-and-services exports also hit an all-time high.
items.title: India's October Merchandise Exports Hit Record High Amid Rising Oil Imports

items.summary: Police and the Special Operations Group busted a fake-currency operation in Shahjahanpur, Uttar Pradesh, arresting Reena, Akil, Suhail, Imran and Ashutosh while recovering counterfeit notes worth Rs 1.15 lakh plus Rs 37,000 in genuine currency. The gang printed fake Rs 500 notes on GSM paper using portable equipment taught online.
items.title: Counterfeit currency racket busted in Shahjahanpur; Rs 1.15 lakh seized, five arrested

items.summary: A UN official warned that rising attacks on commercial shipping near the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab threaten global peace, stability and economic security. Khaled Khiari told the Security Council that maritime incidents have increased, with October recording the highest monthly toll since February per the International Maritime Organization (IMO), which logged 134 confirmed incidents as of November 11. Twenty-five seafarers were killed. Restrictions raised energy, transport and insurance costs while threatening food security amid constrained fertilizer shipments. Though much energy export capacity has recovered through alternative routes, Khiari cautioned that this does not signal a return to normal conditions. He urged Iran and the United States to pursue good-faith diplomacy in Doha, warning against using chokepoints as instruments of coercion.
items.title: UN Urges Restoration of Safe Navigation in Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea

items.summary: Two readers respond to an article about UK public bodies overwhelmed by chatbot-produced complaints. A nine-year housing-association complaint investigator describes how the role has changed dramatically, noting that hundreds of pages of wordy submissions now arrive and that customers often cannot follow the technical language used in their own letters; she argues human-written complaints are more useful because they reveal genuine need. She adds that AI lets regular complainants flood her organisation with multiple large monthly submissions, which makes staff feel disrespected and prompts plans to treat this as harassment.
items.title: How it feels to battle with a flood of AI-generated complaints

items.summary: On Nov. 14, 2026 Türkiye published a law ratifying the Aug. 7, 2026 Mecca Agreement for Joint Defense between Türkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia. The parliament approved it with 279 votes to 119 among 398 lawmakers present in the 592-member body. Under the pact, the three nations pledged collective security, deeper defense cooperation and regional stability.
items.title: Türkiye Ratifies Mecca Joint Defense Pact With Pakistan and Saudi Arabia

items.summary: Volkswagen reportedly filed trademarks for 'ID. UP' on October 22, 2026, potentially naming its upcoming €20,000 ($22,000) entry-level electric car launching in 2027. The model will use a 37 kWh LFP battery and seat four passengers with 305 liters of luggage space.
items.title: Volkswagen's Next Affordable EV May Be Named ID. UP

items.summary: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick agreed to voluntarily testify before the Senate Banking Committee over concerns about export controls on Nvidia’s advanced chips and an investigation into Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based company allegedly linked to China. Senator Tim Scott requested his appearance for oversight of national security issues surrounding semiconductor exports.
items.title: US Commerce Secretary Lutnick agrees to testify before Senate panel over Nvidia chip export controls

items.summary: A Microsoft outage lasting roughly 18 hours disrupted millions globally, with experts warning costs could reach billions and force small businesses to close. The company called it a technical issue unrelated to cyber-attacks or AI agents. Australia's reliance on foreign technology drew sharp criticism from the Australian Computer Society and AMA, which noted hospitals fell back to paper scripts while courts in South Australia and Victoria were affected.
items.title: Microsoft Outage Threatens Australian Economy Amid Global Disruption

items.summary: On Friday, Elon Musk publicly backed a petition to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO. This follows Huang's resignation amid scrutiny over alleged extramarital relationships, including one with Kimberly Powell and another involving Alice Huang, whom US intelligence officials suspect of ties to Chinese services. Trump also voiced support.
items.title: Elon Musk Backs Petition for Jensen Huang's Nvidia Reinstatement Amid Extramarital Controversy

items.summary: This Finshots Weekly Wrapup examines several global and Indian economic developments. It explores China's consumer subsidies amid pandemic-related property market weakness, job concerns, and an ageing population that have suppressed household spending. The defence-tech landscape is shifting as firms like SpaceX, Palantir, and Anduril raise private capital while renting technology to militaries; India saw startup funding more than double to $282.5 million in 2025. On Nvidia, Jensen Huang stepped down on November 12th amid reports linking him to Alice Huang, causing shares to fall around 30% and wiping out over $1.5 trillion from market value. Separately, India's tyre companies report record revenues but shrinking profits due to rising rubber and crude oil costs compounded by a weaker rupee.
items.title: Nvidia's leadership crisis and India's economic shifts in this week's financial wrapup

items.summary: Tesla opened preorders for the personal-use Cybercab at $29,990 plus a mandatory $299 monthly Autonomy Subscription, with delivery slated for December 2026 in Austin. The vehicle requires an unsupervised subscription to operate inside Tesla's Robotaxi geofences covering eight cities across Texas and Florida; elsewhere it is inert. Independent tracker Koby Pierce found actual service areas cover only 59% to 78% of advertised zones, with rail crossings limiting routing. NHTSA has also ordered Tesla to justify a brake pedal under oath.
items.title: Tesla Cybercab Preorders Open With Mandatory Subscription and Limited Robotaxi Coverage

items.summary: For almost 24 hours, users worldwide could not access Microsoft Teams, Outlook or Copilot, disrupting work, communication and email. The outage affected more than 70 countries and spilled into India's customer-facing operations, including airline email support. Microsoft apologized to customers and partners while ruling out a cyberattack or AI-agent issues as the cause. It attributed the disruption to a technical failure linked to an earlier network capacity upgrade, without providing a full restoration timeline.
items.title: Microsoft Apologizes for Nearly 24-Hour Global Outage Affecting Teams, Outlook and Copilot

items.summary: In a December 1, 2007 Inc. magazine interview, Elon Musk argued that concentrating resources is safer than diversifying when you control the outcome. He had already invested his entire PayPal payout into early-stage SpaceX and Tesla, retaining majority operational authority rather than ceding direction to investors. This challenges conventional advice against single-venture risk: for Musk, actively steering a high-risk venture reduces danger because he solves problems directly.
items.title: Elon Musk's 'eggs in one basket' quote on controlled concentration vs. diversification

items.summary: Daniel Block of Foreign Affairs says the reason US President Donald Trump ignored repeated warnings that NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang was linked to Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive tied to Chinese state security, remains largely speculative. One dominant theory is that Trump wanted to protect NVIDIA and avoid market disruption.
items.title: Why Trump May Have Shielded NVIDIA Despite Spy Warnings

items.summary: Following reports of CEO Jensen Huang's resignation amid allegations involving extramarital relationships, Nvidia's board has approached British chipmaker Arm Holdings' chief executive Rene Haas as a potential successor. The company says its succession process remains early-stage and that it is selecting a search firm without formally engaging candidates. Colette Kress serves as interim CEO.
items.title: Nvidia Board Considers Arm's Rene Haas as Jensen Huang Successor

items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Friday that four agencies—Treasury, the Pentagon, State and USTR—had favored blacklisting Singapore firm Megaspeed on Commerce's entity list but deferred to Commerce. Senator John Curtis questioned whether Commerce serves American interests; Democratic Sen. Richard Blumenthal demanded Lutnick leave office over alleged stalling of Trump's chip crackdown amid a spy scandal involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, whose former executive Alice Huang is suspected of spying for China.
items.title: Bessent Blames Lutnick for Not Blacklisting Nvidia Partner Megaspeed

items.summary: Jensen Huang stepped down as Nvidia CEO on Thursday after revelations of extramarital affairs, plunging the chipmaker into crisis and sending shockwaves across an AI industry he helped bankroll. Cristiano Amon (Haas) is among several candidates being considered to succeed him, though there is no guarantee he will be offered or accept the role. Reuters could not independently verify the report.
items.title: Nvidia Seeks Successor for Jensen Huang Amid Leadership Crisis

items.summary: Anthropic is launching an invite-only IPO, raising up to $90.4 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation on the Nasdaq under symbol ANT, led by Morgan Stanley with 20 other banks. Prospective investors in mainland China and Hong Kong face restrictions: some banks refused orders or deemed allocations unlikely, partly due to US International Traffic in Arms Regulations. This mirrors SpaceX's $86.2 billion IPO, which barred Chinese buyers from accepting orders but allowed post-listing purchases. Anthropic offers shares only in Australia, Canada, EEA members, Japan, Switzerland and the UK. Despite an AI-related selloff, demand is intense—investors seek about six times available shares, with some offering allocations to new investors.
items.title: Anthropic's Invite-Only IPO Faces China Access Restrictions and Record Investor Demand

items.summary: Business Network International (BNI) CEO Mary Kennedy Thompson argues that human connections remain essential as artificial intelligence automates functions like accounting, finance and marketing. She predicts the world's first billionaire solopreneur may emerge within five years, yet insists solo operators still need trusted networks because people prefer doing business with those they know. AI makes genuine capability harder to verify, so proof points from organizations like BNI will grow faster. Thompson cites strong returns—US$71 (S$91) in closed business per US$1 spent—and notes the global network generated over 17 million referrals worth roughly US$27 billion in a year.
items.title: BNI CEO on Human Connections in an AI-Driven Business Era

items.summary: On Friday (Nov 13), OpenAI launched the ChatGPT Wallet, enabling its always-on 'dots' agents to pay for purchases without exposing users' card details. Built with American Express, Mastercard and Visa, it launches in the US for Pro subscribers aged 18+ with eligible cards. Each transaction requires a security check—Face ID or fingerprint—and shows items, total and selected card first.
items.title: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Wallet for AI-Powered Payments

items.summary: Following the November 2026 US midterms, which voters interpreted as a mandate to regulate AI more aggressively, Richard Reisman argues that efforts to make technology pro-human must be treated as one integrated challenge rather than siloed problems. He identifies three core disconnects: AI and social media are merging into an inseparable system; both ignore humanity's rich social nature; and remediation requires a whole-of-society project. To address these, Reisman proposes five framing principles — thought as a social process, three mutually reinforcing pillars of healthy discourse (individual agency, social mediation, reputation/trust) linked by open interoperability, negotiated access to attention and data via reverse metering, personal AI advocate agents that serve users loyally, and an overarching test question: who does it serve? He frames the solution as a broad 'big-tent' alliance, pointing to the newly formed Pro-Human AI Coalition (60 organizations) alongside earlier work by Project Liberty and the Social Web Foundation. Reisman acknowledges these are wicked problems with no silver bullet, noting that dominant platforms underweight public good while policy has lagged.
items.title: Making AI and Social Media Pro-Human Through a Big-Tent Alliance

items.summary: US company SpaceX launched its latest Starship flight into orbit on Friday, though it did not recover the booster as planned; instead, the booster exploded over the Gulf of Mexico. The upper stage reached orbit and is scheduled to return Saturday for capture by mechanical arms—marking a first attempt at recovery. This uncrewed test aims to develop full reusability to cut spaceflight costs.
items.title: SpaceX Launches Starship but Fails Booster Recovery

items.summary: "Tech Now" is a podcast series covering technology across many domains and locations. Episodes feature journalists visiting sites such as Cairngorms National Park, Pokémon World Championships in San Francisco, Iceland's solar eclipse research, Microsoft's Quantum Lab in Denmark, Esrange Spaceport in Sweden, Fifa HQ in Zurich, MWC Barcelona, CES 2026 in Las Vegas, Oslo's Olympic training centre, and the Arctic. Topics span wildfires, counterfeit detection, assisted births, prosthetics, heart surgery, underwater tech, AI art analysis, climate science litigation, insect farming, green tourism, esports, WWE production, supercomputing, shipwreck preservation, fashion sizing via AI, and space exploration robots."
items.title: Tech Now

items.summary: India's Nifty IT index lost momentum, falling nearly 2% in November after October gains. Despite AI-heavy bets plunging across Asia and new opportunities from sectoral churn, legacy IT stocks stagnate amid earnings concerns at outsourcing firms. September-quarter results show uneven recovery with mid-tier players outperforming larger peers by roughly five times on sequential revenue growth (5.4% vs 1.1%). Kotak estimates gross deflation of around 7%, while Infosys may cut FY27 guidance to 1.5-2.5%. Pricing pressure and AI investments weigh on profitability, though integration complexity offers fresh opportunities in data engineering and cybersecurity.
items.title: AI Relief Fails to Lift Legacy IT Stocks as Earnings Worries Weigh

items.summary: After a 13-year wait, Grand Theft Auto 6 is launching soon, yet even co-creator Dave Jones and original writer Brian Baglow have not played it. The article traces the series' origins to DMA Design's 1997 debut in Dundee, Scotland, which pioneered on-foot car-stealing gameplay and spawned word-of-mouth success despite controversy partly manufactured by publisher BMG Interactive. GTA V later earned $1bn (£760m) within three days of its 2013 launch. Guardian editor Keza MacDonald notes films now draw more from the series than vice, reflecting its real-life grounding.
items.title: GTA's Original Creators Still Waiting on GTA 6 as Series Becomes Cultural Phenomenon

items.summary: The FAA cancelled a rare nationwide ground stop on Friday evening after a communications outage grounded thousands of flights, leaving tens of thousands of passengers stranded. More than 4,700 flights were cancelled and 10,000 delayed, with another 700 already cancelled for Saturday.
items.title: US Lifts Nationwide Air Ground Stop After Communications Outage Chaos

items.summary: President Museveni's son, Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, is fueling succession speculation as he arrests senior military officers amid tensions over who will succeed the 82-year-old ruler. Analysts split on whether the crackdown targets anti-Kainerugaba officers or addresses corruption; some detainees have been released after his forgiveness. Kainerugaba's social media threats against Vice-President Alupo and controversial posts drew diplomatic controversy before his account was suspended. The debate intensifies as Museveni considers retiring in 2031, with competing candidates emerging within the ruling party.
items.title: Uganda's Succession Crisis and Kainerugaba Crackdown

items.summary: On Friday afternoon of November 13, 2026, the FAA ordered a nationwide suspension of domestic flights at around 4 p.m. Eastern Time, citing extraordinary circumstances and security concerns after air traffic control communications failed across radar systems and radio frequencies. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy confirmed the disruption while officials investigated; Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin ruled out criminal activity or malicious attack but declined to speculate on duration. FlightAware reported roughly 2,630 canceled flights and more than 26,100 delayed domestically, with over 3,000 still arriving at airports around 4:30 p.m.
items.title: Nationwide US Flight Grounding Over Air Traffic Control Communications Failure

items.summary: Forecasting weather in the Southern Hemisphere is harder than in the north due to less land mass, fewer surface observations and weather balloons, plus more people and funding concentrated up north. The gap has narrowed recently as satellite data now supplies over 90 per cent of forecast information, with Australia relying on about 40 satellites owned by countries including the US and Japan delivering roughly 13.5–14 million observations daily. Forecasters are also adopting AI, such as Google DeepMind's system shown in 2024 to predict weather 15 days ahead more accurately than existing systems, while improving extreme-event forecasting for cyclones and atmospheric rivers that caused the Brisbane and Lismore floods.
items.title: Why Southern Hemisphere Weather Forecasting Remains Challenging and How It Is Improving

items.summary: A rare grounding halted all departing flights across the United States on Friday, stranding hundreds of thousands amid confusion over cause. Officials blamed a telecommunications outage affecting air traffic control communications, with no indication of an attack. Flights already airborne continued to their destinations while authorities coordinated safe landings.
items.title: ‘One more extra day away from the kids’: Stranded travellers react to the Friday the 13th chaos at US airports

items.summary: An internet trade group, NetChoice, sued New York in federal court on Friday, seeking to block a state law requiring social media platforms with infinite scrolling, auto-play and algorithmic feeds to display warning labels for younger users. NetChoice argues the law violates First Amendment protections by compelling its members—over 30 companies including Google, Meta and Snap—to convey the state's preferred message about online safety.
items.title: NetChoice Sues New York Over Social Media Warning-Label Law

items.summary: On the occasion of Jawaharlal Nehru's 137th birth anniversary, Arvind Narrain reframes contemporary political prisoners—Umar Khalid (six years jailed), Sudha Bharadwaj, Anand Teltumbde, Sharjeel Imam, Arun Ferreira and Seema Azad—as heirs to the Nehru of colonial prison days. Rather than defaulting to the Emergency as analogy for Modi's 'undeclared emergency,' the author points to colonial rule itself: a regime defined by pervasive fear and naked coercion that Nehru exposed as self-defeating. Drawing on his Autobiography, Discovery of India and Glimpses of World History—written from prison across more than nine years—Nehru emerges not only as a philosopher of resistance but also of living with dignity amid struggle.
items.title: Nehru as a Guide to India's Undeclared Emergency

items.summary: The Maharashtra Forest Department has rejected Adani Green Energy Ltd's revised cost of ₹56.75 crore for its 1,500 MW Tarali pumped storage project in Satara, insisting the total remains ₹5,675 crore and demanding supporting documents.
items.title: Maharashtra Forest Department Questions Adani's Tarali Project Cost Revision

items.summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari mocked former leader Mamata Banerjee, claiming she faced the wrath of Maa Kali after an idol was carried in a prison van during Mahalaya. While addressing festival celebrations across North and South 24 Parganas districts, Chandannagar and other towns, he highlighted growing religious participation.
items.title: West Bengal CM Adhikari Mocks Mamata Over Delhi Detention Amid Festival Address

items.summary: Pakistan held off Sri Lanka for a first-in-series draw in Rawalpindi, with Saud Shakeel scoring 97 to fall three short of his second century. His twin nineties scores made him only the sixth batter ever dismissed between 90 and 99 in both innings of one Test, following Clem Hill (1902), Frank Woolley (1921), Gordon Greenidge (twice) and Mahela Jayawardene (2009). Pakistan's World Test Championship form remains poor: seven defeats against two wins from nine matches. The second Test moves to Rawalpindi next Tuesday, shifted from Lahore due to smog.
items.title: Saud Shakeel joins rare Test batting record list after near-century draw vs Sri Lanka

items.summary: A telecommunications outage disrupted air traffic control across the United States on Friday, forcing the FAA to halt departures nationwide. Overloaded switches and routers in an ageing system triggered inconsistent data and radar failures affecting all 22 regional centres. More than 4,000 flights were cancelled and over 10,000 delayed, stranding roughly 1.5 million passengers.
items.title: US FAA Outage Grounds Nationwide Flights After Telecom Failure

items.summary: The Delhi High Court directed subject experts to review four disputed answers in the UGC-NET June 2026 answer key, warning that errors can affect candidates' merit ranking and eligibility. A bench led by Justice Jasmeet Singh declined to interfere with six of ten challenged questions but referred the remaining four—two from Education-009, one Urdu, one Geography—for a reasoned decision within three weeks. The exam drew about 727,506 candidates; its English paper faced criticism after 67 of 150 questions were reportedly repeated.
items.title: Delhi HC Orders Review of UGC-NET June 2026 Answer Key Over Reported Errors

items.summary: On Friday evening, sirens sounded at RAF Lakenheath in Suffolk and RAF Feltwell in Norfolk around 5.30 pm local time (0430 GMT), which some residents likened to wartime warnings. A loudspeaker announcement in an American accent urged people indoors; video showed alarms across darkened gardens. The US Air Force confirmed the alarm linked suspected unauthorized drones, with no personnel, aircraft or infrastructure affected.
items.title: Sirens Sound at UK Air Bases Over Suspected Drone Activity

items.summary: Microsoft announced that its consumer products services had fully recovered at 4:10 p.m. UTC on Friday, November 16, 2026 (GMT). In contrast, the company reported only sustained recovery for Microsoft 365 enterprise services and stated it was monitoring a backlog of email messages accrued during the incident before considering that issue resolved. Citing the severity of the impact, Microsoft said it would continue monitoring for an extended period to ensure no additional mitigative actions were required.
items.title: Microsoft Reports Consumer Services Recovery; Enterprise Still Being Monitored

items.summary: On November 13 at 4:10 p.m. UTC (Friday), Microsoft announced its consumer products services had fully recovered, while noting only sustained recovery for its Microsoft 365 enterprise services. The company stated it was monitoring the backlog of email messages accrued during the incident before considering the issue resolved, and emphasized continued observation due to the severity of impact caused by the event.
items.title: Microsoft says consumer products services recovered; still monitoring enterprise services

items.summary: Tesla invited select customers to place orders for the driverless two-seat Cybercab, which lacks a steering wheel and pedals, expanding from its Austin robotaxi service into limited consumer availability. Individual reservations cost $29,990 plus a required $299 monthly subscription. Tesla's AI head Ashok Elluswamy said it will operate unsupervised across the same areas as the fleet, though regulators may still intervene; an NHTSA probe opened shortly after its September debut.
items.title: Tesla Opens Cybercab Orders to Select Customers

items.summary: As President Trump prepares to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping next week, lawmakers on both sides of Congress are pressing for tighter restrictions on technology exports amid the Nvidia scandal. Analysts say the affair encapsulates U.S.-China rivalry over AI chips and national security. The strategy in Washington has been focused on controlling where California-based Nvidia's best chips go. But China hawks now have a story with a name and a face to support their argument, while Beijing warns against using the episode as a pretext for new restrictions.
items.title: The Nvidia Scandal's China Chip Fallout

items.summary: An analyst argues that China's trade surplus is often misread through the lens of zero-sum competition, using Vietnam as an illustrative case. Despite widening deficits with China and other ASEAN economies, Vietnam grew 9.95% in GDP while its exports rose 24.5%. The article attributes these patterns to comparative advantage: imported machinery and components enable domestic manufacturing that generates finished-goods exports. It notes China's own import surges—storage components up 150%, integrated circuits up 56.6%—reflecting demand for intermediate products, while services trade runs a deficit of 1.23 trillion yuan in nine months. The piece concludes that trade balances alone cannot capture economic relations; supply-chain integration and investment matter equally.
items.title: China's Trade Surplus as a Misunderstood Narrative

items.summary: A global outage lasting over 24 hours knocked out Microsoft products, including Outlook and Teams, across 74 countries. Singapore's government Outlook services were fully restored by Friday night at 11pm per GovTech. Emergency services remained operational while Singpass was unaffected. Banks such as UOB and DBS, along with SingHealth, confirmed email restoration, though some replies may be delayed.
items.title: Singapore Government Outlook Services Restored After Global Microsoft Outage

items.summary: On Friday Microsoft reported that its consumer products and services had fully recovered, while Microsoft 365 enterprise services showed only partial recovery with no timeline for full restoration. A global outage of Outlook and Teams, which disrupted communications across businesses and governments after more than 24 hours, was easing but remained unresolved. The company attributed the incident to server issues rather than malicious activity or AI.
items.title: Microsoft Consumer Products Services Recover After Global Outage

items.summary: The JioBlackRock Flexi Cap Fund trimmed its holdings, selling ITC shares worth Rs 10.92 crore and exiting 17 stocks including Yes Bank (1.82 crore shares), Billionbrains Garage Ventures, CESC, REC and Hindalco Industries. It added Punjab National Bank and increased exposure across 27 stocks while holding 129 in October versus a September AUM of Rs 3,149 crore.
items.title: JioBlackRock Flexi Cap Fund Portfolio Changes in October

items.summary: Microsoft's November 12, 2026 outage degraded its services for over 10 hours and reached at least 74 countries, with complaints peaking near 140,000. Impact concentrated in the Americas, Europe and Australia; governments like Germany's BSI and Australia activated recovery measures. China was largely unaffected because Microsoft 365 there runs on isolated domestic infrastructure via 21Vianet, while agencies migrate to alternatives by 2027 under laws like the Cybersecurity Law. Yet concentration risk persists across Alibaba Cloud, Huawei Cloud and Tencent Cloud—true sovereignty requires interoperability and exit strategies.
items.title: The Microsoft Outage China Barely Felt: A Lesson on Data Sovereignty

items.summary: Nvidia founder Jensen Huang is leaving the company, forfeiting roughly $108 million in unvested restricted stock units. This represents just 0.07% of his estimated $144.5 billion net worth, which remains overwhelmingly tied to his ~812 million Nvidia shares valued at about $135 billion—nearly 97% of his fortune and making him the company's largest individual shareholder. His departure coincides with Nvidia's market value falling below $4 trillion for the first time since 2025, though his existing holdings remain largely intact.
items.title: Jensen Huang's Nvidia Exit and Remaining Wealth

items.summary: Elon Musk signed a petition to reinstate Jensen Huang, who resigned amid scrutiny over alleged extramarital relationships, including one with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman suspected of links to Chinese intelligence services. The controversy drew support from President Donald Trump and Musk, who has emphasized the importance of company founders. Questions persist about Huang's personal conduct and leadership at Nvidia, where he co-founded the AI chip supplier in 1993.
items.title: Musk Endorses Move to Reinstate Huang at Nvidia

items.summary: A Bloomberg investigation details how U.S.-restricted Nvidia AI chips reached a large Shanghai data center. Singapore-based Aperia bought 22 Dell servers with H800 chips, which were later shipped to Shanghai and installed in Alice Huang's company. Documents show 193 servers pledged as loan collateral worth ¥485 million (~$73 million), including 52 Super Micro servers containing H100/H200 chips requiring U.S. licenses.
items.title: चीन में एलिस हुआंग की कंपनी तक कैसे पहुंचे प्रतिबंधित Nvidia चिप्स? AI डेटा सेंटर से खुला राज

items.summary: A worldwide outage of Microsoft's Outlook, Teams, and Microsoft 365 lasted over 15 hours starting November 12. Microsoft attributed it to failing servers under network pressure, not an attack—no evidence links OpenAI or Anthropic agents to the incident.
items.title: Microsoft Outage and AI Attack Speculation

items.summary: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told senior executives, including general counsel Tim Teter and chief marketing officer Alison Wagonfeld, that his relationship with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang was routine business. The two people are not related but share a surname. After press scrutiny, an independent probe by law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz launched. Beijing denies she is a spy; Reuters has not verified it. Huang resigned as CEO Thursday and apologized for being unfaithful without naming Alice Huang. Nvidia's stock fell more than 30% from its October 6 high, wiping out over $1.8 trillion in market capitalisation.
items.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang misled executives over affair with Alice Huang; resigns amid scandal

items.summary: Microsoft reported that its consumer products services had fully recovered at 4:10 p.m. UTC on Friday, while Microsoft 365 enterprise services were still experiencing sustained recovery. The company said it was monitoring the backlog of email messages accrued during the event and noted that, due to the severity of the incident's impact, it would continue monitoring for an extended period to ensure no additional mitigative actions are required.
items.title: Microsoft Restores Consumer Services After Outage

items.summary: Microsoft apologised after a global outage disrupted Teams, Outlook and Copilot AI for nearly a day across more than 70 countries. The company ruled out a cyberattack, attributing the disruption to a technical fault from an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced after a later change. Services were restored gradually amid airline and business disruptions in India.
items.title: Microsoft Apologises for Global Outage, Rules Out Cyberattack

items.summary: A Trump administration official running U.S. export control programs sought marquee speakers for the Bureau of Industry and Security's annual conference, considering Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang as an unusual option. Under Secretary of Commerce Jeffrey Kessler had expressed interest in inviting Huang to speak on Jan. 10 in Washington, braging about his ability to secure attendance before the then-Nvidia chief fell out of consideration.
items.title: Nvidia Crisis Sparks Scrutiny of Agency Overseeing Chip Curbs

items.summary: Elon Musk endorsed a petition seeking the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO, commenting days after Huang's reported resignation amid allegations involving his personal relationships. His support joins backing from figures including President Donald Trump. The controversy centers on reports that Huang had extramarital relationships with Kimberly Powell and Alice Huang, raising national security concerns given her suspected ties to Chinese intelligence services.
items.title: Elon Musk Backs Petition to Reinstate Jensen Huang at Nvidia

items.summary: Nvidia's board has approached Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas as a potential successor to Jensen Huang, who resigned amid scrutiny over alleged extramarital relationships. The Financial Times reported the move following his departure after 33 years at the helm. Nvidia says succession is still in early stages and calls candidate speculation premature; CFO Colette Kress serves as interim CEO while employees back a petition for Huang's return.
items.title: Who Could Replace Jensen Huang At Nvidia? Arm CEO Rene Haas Emerges As Potential Successor

items.summary: A significant share of the world's displays traces back to China's Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, particularly Shenzhen. From phone screens to giant city skyline displays, the entire supply chain—from display panels to LED modules—sits within a few hours' drive, enabling rapid scaling. CGTN's Wang Tianyu investigated how Shenzhen leverages this geographic advantage to serve customers worldwide.
items.title: Shenzhen Lights Up the Asia-Pacific Display Industry

items.summary: A migrant caravan of about 1,500 people—mostly Hondurans, with several dozen Nicaraguans, roughly 100 Guatemalans, plus Haitians, Venezuelans, Cubans, Ecuadorians, and one Turk—has halted in Huixtla after advancing only ~80 kilometers from the border. Activist Luis Villagrán counts it as the 24th caravan to leave Chiapas this year; Mexico's government says it is the 10th. Trump threatened to immediately double tariffs on Mexico unless migrants are stopped, warning that pressure could force President Sheinbaum to send caravans back—a fear Vanega calls 'the real terror.' Meanwhile, U.S. migration policy remains unchanged after midterms, though Texas's Republican governor Greg Abbott has fortified the border over 12 years.
items.title: Mexico's Migrant Caravan and Trump's Tariff Threat

items.summary: Google Fellow Vahab Mirrokni announced results from Antigravity's /teamwork multiagent systems, which enhance human-AI collaboration to solve open problems in mathematics, chemistry, systems software, and ML engineering. The system addresses two model limitations: unpredictable generation by pairing parallel exploration with dedicated falsifiers like the Lean 4 proof checker, and attention dispersion over long tasks via context partitioning where coordinators hand off to fresh agents from clean contexts. Researchers paired with Gemini 4 models proved information theory's Courtade–Kumar conjecture in full generality using /teamwork's Long Proof pattern, formalizing it into 50 million lines of Lean code.
items.title: Google's Antigravity /teamwork Multiagent Systems Advance Science and Engineering

items.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar, speaking at the Hindustan Times Leadership Summit 2026, said the US-India trade deal is expected to close soon. He noted that most issues are sorted and remaining concerns lie more on the American side than New Delhi's, with hopes of concluding it shortly. Negotiators typically withhold such details during talks.
items.title: Jaishankar on India-US Trade Deal Progress at HT Leadership Summit 2026

items.summary: Li Haitao, dean of Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business, frames AI-driven cooperation in the Asia-Pacific as a “multiplication effect.” Along the Mekong River, a young Vietnamese operator uses a Chinese smart drone to deliver precision agricultural services to local farmers. In one flight, this simple technology links Chinese innovation, Vietnamese farmland and regional markets, turning broad regional-cooperation goals into tangible benefits for communities on the ground.
items.title: Li Haitao on AI Cooperation as a Multiplication Effect

items.summary: On the second day of Chhath Puja, BJP leader Pradeep Bhandari criticized Congress's Rahul Gandhi over remarks from last year's festival. Sharing a one-year-old clip in which Gandhi called "Chhath Puja" a drama, Bhandari demanded a public apology and accused him of disrespecting Hindu sentiments and the people of Bihar. The attack followed Maharashtra Navnirman Sena chief Raj Thackeray accusing BJP of using Chhath Puja reels to sow discord in Maharashtra.
items.title: 'Chhath Puja not drama': BJP rakes up year-old video to target Rahul Gandhi

items.summary: On Jawaharlal Nehru's 137th birth anniversary—also Children's Day in India (s0)—PM Narendra Modi paid tribute via X, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh recalled his role in the freedom struggle and early independent-India leadership, and opposition leader Rahul Gandhi called him 'jewel of India,' emphasizing Swaraj as citizens' participation. Nehru was born November 14, 1889, died May 27, 1964 (s10), became first PM August 15, 1947 (s11). Schools and government bodies hold commemorative events; the UN declared Universal Children's Day on November 20 in 1954, while India marked his birthday as National Children's Day from 1964 onward (s8-s16).
items.title: 'Jewel of India': PM Modi, Rahul Gandhi, Rajnath Singh pay tributes to Nehru on birth anniversary

items.summary: US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick faces mounting pressure from lawmakers over the Trump administration's handling of the Nvidia scandal, which began with revelations that a Megaspeed executive accused of ties to Chinese intelligence had an affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Multiple Republican senators have called for both Lutnick and Huang to testify before Congress as investigations continue.
items.title: US Commerce Secretary in Spotlight Over Nvidia Scandal

items.summary: Nvidia's founder and co-founder Jensen Huang resigned Thursday amid an affair with a woman US officials believe worked for Chinese intelligence, plus reports of a second relationship. CFO Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while Harvey Jones becomes the board's first chair; no succession plan exists. Investors may discount Nvidia's leadership premium, though some see AI leadership broadening to rivals like AMD and Broadcom. The resignation risks contagion across the AI funding loop just before Anthropic's IPO. Huang championed European projects in Germany and Sweden and advised President Trump on chip exports to China, whose influence may now wane.
items.title: What is next for Nvidia after CEO Jensen Huang resigns?

items.summary: Comfort, a blind Nigerian pensioner who has lived in the UK since 2000 and arrived here 26 years ago, was told by the Home Office she could return to Nigeria. Under new settlement rules announced by Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood, her path to indefinite leave to remain now extends roughly two decades until her 80s. Lawyers at Refugee and Migrant Justice sought an exception on disability grounds, but their request was refused. Nick Beales of the charity condemned the policy as cruel, noting decision-makers conflated India with Nigeria.
items.title: UK Home Office Rejects Settlement for Blind Nigerian Pensioner; Rights Groups Criticize New Rules

items.summary: The FAA grounded all US departures for over four hours on Friday after a communications failure overloaded aging air traffic control routers, cancelling 6,600 flights and delaying 8,600. Secretary Sean Duffy reopened airspace at 8:15pm but blamed Congress for underfunding the system.
items.title: US Nationwide FAA Ground Stop Lifted After Communications Failure Chaos

items.summary: The White House announced that Trump, Putin and Xi Jinping will hold a historic joint summit on the sidelines of next week's Apec summit in Shenzhen. Topics may include global nuclear weapons reduction and Iran, though Ukraine is off the agenda. The trip also includes an ASEAN summit in the Philippines. No agreement is expected to follow the talks.
items.title: Trump, Putin and Xi plan historic trilateral meeting in Shenzhen

items.summary: Central European University (CEU), forced by Viktor Orbán's government to relocate its teaching operations from Budapest to Vienna in 2019, is signaling renewed interest in expanding its presence in the capital as a confidence vote in Hungary's democratic future. Interim president Carsten Q Schneider says no formal talks have occurred with Péter Magyar's new Tisza-led government yet, but both sides are reaching out. The university retains only administrative staff and 312 employees in Budapest; teaching remains centered in Vienna amid concerns about student mobility across the distance.
items.title: CEU Reaches Out to Hungary's New Government After Orbán Era

items.summary: Against the backdrop of Gen Z protests across Germany and Europe, DW examines whether young people face greater challenges than Baby Boomers did in the 1990s. Youth researcher Simon Schnetzer argues both generations share difficult conditions and must unite for constructive reform. The article surveys pensions, housing, education and climate change. Pension contributors per retiree fell from 3.73 in 1957 to 2.1 by 2025, projected at 1.73 by 2045, with €118 billion [$131 billion]—about 25% of the federal budget—in subsidies. Housing costs rose sharply for low-income households; rent share climbed from ~24% in 1990 to nearly 36% in 2021. Public education spending doubled since 2011, yet Germany ranks mid-tier internationally and faces a projected teacher shortfall of around 27,000 by 2035. Climate projections warn children today may face heat waves two to seven times more often than Boomers.
items.title: Do Baby Boomers Have It Better Than Gen Z? A German Data Comparison

items.summary: China has warned the United States against tightening chip export controls, saying Beijing opposes their abuse and calls allegations a technological blockade pretext. A company founded by Alice Huang reportedly obtained Nvidia H800 chips banned since 2023 via Dell servers bought through Singapore partner Aperia Cloud Services. The row intensifies US lawmaker pressure ahead of an expected Trump-Xi meeting at the Shenzhen APEC summit.
items.title: China Warns US Over Chip Curbs as Suspected Spy's Firm Got Banned Chips

items.summary: As of October 31, 2026, nine equity mutual funds surpassed Rs 70,000 crore in assets under management (AUM), with the top four each exceeding Rs 1 lakh crore. Parag Parikh Flexi Cap Fund led at Rs 1.46 lakh crore; HDFC's three funds ranged from Rs 1.10 to Rs 1.00 lakh crore, followed by SBI Aggressive Hybrid (Rs 85,922 crore), Nippon India Small Cap (Rs 76,902 crore), ICICI Pru Large Cap (Rs 76,895 crore), Kotak Arbitrage (Rs 76,415 crore) and ICICI Pru Balanced Advantage (Rs 71,892 crore).
items.title: Nine Equity Mutual Funds Cross Rs 70,000 Crore AUM as of October 31, 2026

items.summary: The FAA ended the longest nationwide flight ground stop since September 2001, lasting over four hours due to an overloaded legacy air traffic control communications system. More than 8,500 flights were delayed and nearly 8,000 cancelled. Officials ruled out a cyber-attack or link to Microsoft's outage.
items.title: Longest US Ground Stop Since 9/11 Lifted After Communication Outage

items.summary: The US resumed air traffic Friday after a nearly five-hour nationwide halt caused by instability in the aging FAA communications system, which forced more than 6,500 flight cancellations and about 10,000 delays. The problem began around 3:36 p.m. Eastern as new equipment overloads were integrated into outdated infrastructure; authorities ruled out sabotage or cyberattacks and called it a precautionary measure. Officials blamed decades-old technology and urged Congress for $50 billion in emergency funding to build a replacement system, which is expected to cost roughly $31.5 billion.
items.title: US Air Traffic Resumes After Nearly Five-Hour Computer-System Shutdown

items.summary: Thousands gathered for the 94th Adelaide Christmas Pageant, marking the festive season's start. Organisers estimate about 335,000 people attended as Father Christmas arrived to close proceedings. The Magic Cave attraction remains open despite David Jones entering voluntary administration and closing stores across Australia and New Zealand.
items.title: Adelaide Christmas Pageant Draws Estimated 335,000 Amid David Jones Collapse

items.summary: A preliminary probe into the November 11 derailment of the Kolkata-Sairang Express near Guwahati points to a malfunctioning main braking system, with questions raised over whether crew conducted mandatory brake feel and power tests. Officials suggest station staff isolated the brake pipe angle cock under an outdated locomotive-change procedure after electrification ended that practice. The Railway Board has directed all zonal railways to conduct these two tests post-handover and ordered a safety drive from November 12-18, with discrepancies reported by November 20.
items.title: Kolkata-Sairang Express Derailment Probe Points to Brake Failure and Missed Safety Checks

items.summary: On the evening of 14 September, Mahli Beardman, a 21-year-old fast bowler from Dampier in Western Australia's Pilbara region, produced what is billed as the best-ever Australian ODI debut performance. Playing against England at just six runs to his name while conceding only two wickets (6/24), he also helped Australia post 8/294 versus Zimbabwe. His remarkable figures are being hailed as a cause for celebration across regional Western Australia and hoped to inspire the next generation of country cricketers.
items.title: Mahli Beardman's Record-Breaking ODI Debut Hauls Six Wickets for Australia vs Zimbabwe

items.summary: President Trump threatened to double tariffs on Mexico unless it halts a migrant caravan heading toward the US border, intensifying tensions with its largest trading partner. Illegal crossings have fallen during his second term as Mexico deployed troops and sought White House favor. Democratic electoral gains raised hopes of more lenient immigration policy, but Stephen Miller's appointment as chief of staff—despite his role in harsh enforcement measures like raids—has undermined those expectations.
items.title: Trump Threatens New Tariffs on Mexican Goods Over Migrant Caravan

items.summary: Opposition Leader Rahul Gandhi arrived in Hyderabad ahead of the Bharat Summit, participating in a large bike rally with gig workers and riding pillion on one worker's scooter. Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy also joined the event. Separately, BJP and Congress leaders are exchanging allegations over central-government phone tapping.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi Joins Gig-Worker Bike Rally in Hyderabad Ahead of Bharat Summit

items.summary: Political tensions have intensified between the BJP and Congress after Rahul Gandhi accused the central government of phone tapping, alleging foreign influence. Union Minister Pralhad Joshi questioned Gandhi's credibility while defending PM Modi's use of teleprompters. Opposition leaders backed Gandhi by recalling past surveillance incidents like Pegasus.
items.title: BJP and Congress Clash Over Rahul Gandhi's Phone Tapping Claims Amid Rising Political Tensions

items.summary: Helle Lyng Svendsen, a Norwegian journalist known for confronting Prime Minister Narendra Modi during his 2025 visit to Norway, alleges the Indian embassy in Oslo revoked her visa moments before she was set to depart for Hyderabad. She had been scheduled as a delegate at the Congress government's Bharat Summit in Telangana. In an interview with Dagsavisen, Svendsen blames Home Minister Amit Shah and claims officials told her the cancellation came 'on orders from above.'
items.title: Norwegian Journalist Blames Home Minister for Visa Cancellation Ahead of Bharat Summit

items.summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari asked 12,000 people who allegedly received Banglar Bari housing funds fraudulently under the previous TMC government to refund them by November 30. Verification reportedly found 57,000 ineligible beneficiaries delisted; around 12,000 had already been paid ₹60,000 each in a second instalment disbursed alongside one million others, totaling ₹10,323 crore to roughly 17.21 lakh eligible recipients.
items.title: West Bengal CM demands refunds from fraudulently aided housing beneficiaries amid scheme probe

items.summary: Brett Easton Ellis’s 1991 novel American Psycho follows Patrick Bateman, an investment banker in 1980s New York City obsessed with appearances while secretly committing murders. Mary Harron’s 2000 film largely replaces the graphic violence with comedy of manners about Wall Street elites, leaving open whether Bateman is a real killer or fantasist.
items.title: American Psycho and the Art of Depicting a Monster

items.summary: Buying a home in India requires an upfront down payment of roughly 10-25% after banks finance up to 90% under RBI LTV rules. Rising prices—up 59% across top seven cities from Rs 5,826 to Rs 9,260 per square foot (2021-2025)—have squeezed buyers. Experts caution against overpaying or draining emergency savings.
items.title: How Much Down Payment Should You Make on a Home?

items.summary: At the National Lawyers Convention of the Federalist Society in Hamilton, Canada on November 14, 2026, Secretary of State Marco Rubio sharply criticized the International Criminal Court (ICC) and the UN. He argued that a global elite uses international law to undermine US sovereignty, citing Trump's order to sink cartel boats and Maduro's capture as examples of accusations against Washington. Defending sanctions on the ICC, he called it an unelected world tribunal accountable to no one.
