items.title: Rubio Attacks ICC and International Law at Federalist Society Address

items.summary: A Madras High Court bench of Justices GR Swaminathan and MD Sumathi ruled on November 12 that a community's inclusion in the Other Backward Classes (OBC) list cannot be treated as permanent or automatically justified merely because it has enjoyed reservation benefits for decades. The court said the Tamil Nadu government must demonstrate, to its satisfaction, the constitutional validity of any challenged inclusion or continued retention whenever someone contests classification. Admitting a petition by G Kodeeswaran challenging provisions in the 2016 Government Servants Act granting Backward Class and Most Backward Class status to several Christian communities and converts, the bench found serious doubts over absent objective data on social and educational backwardness and ignored expert commission recommendations. The petitioner argued conversion could grant OBC benefits even to a Brahmin joining the Church of South India, prompting the court to order a serious re-examination of Tamil Nadu's reservation framework.
items.title: Madras High Court Rules OBC Reservation Inclusion Not Permanent or Self-Justifying

items.summary: This morning briefing covers global developments as of Saturday, November 14, 2026. Türkiye and Qatar signed five agreements in Istanbul, including a mutual defense pact ratified by parliament (279-119). The US FAA lifted a nationwide flight ground stop after a telecom outage; officials called it an emergency but not necessarily a cyberattack, with over 10,000 flights delayed or canceled. Trump will meet Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen at the APEC summit to discuss nuclear weapons reduction. In health news, Nigeria's largest diphtheria outbreak reached 28,151 cases and 1,126 deaths; the US lost its measles elimination status with 5,400 reported cases in 2026.
items.title: Morning Briefing: Nov. 14, 2026

items.summary: SpaceX launched its reusable Starship rocket from Texas on Friday, aiming for a historic double catch but falling short when the Super Heavy booster splashed down in the Gulf of Mexico amid unknown causes. The upper stage continued orbiting at over 26,000 km/h. SpaceX employees cheered as it sought to advance rapid reusability toward lunar and Mars missions.
items.title: SpaceX Starship Test Falls Short of Double-Catch Goal

items.summary: QR codes have become common for business cards, cashless payments and digital links, but creating one often means dealing with slow websites cluttered by ads, sign-up walls and invasive privacy policies that even hijack your links. A new tool called Ente QR offers a simpler alternative: it is free, requires no sign-ups or usage limits, and comes from The Intelligence's Cool Tools newsletter, which emphasizes protecting user data.
items.title: A Simple, Private QR Code Creator

items.summary: Nearly two months after a 17-year-old girl was allegedly gang-raped at knifepoint in Delhi's Astha Kunj Park on her September 22 birthday, police filed a 450-page chargesheet against three accused—Asif, Hemant and Mukesh—at Saket Court. The survivor alleges she was assaulted twice with weapons while her friend was held; the third man is referred to as Deepu.
items.title: Delhi Gang Rape Chargesheet Filed Against Three Accused

items.summary: Sen. Alan Armstrong of Oklahoma hired T. Lane Wilson, a senior vice president and general counsel at the Williams Companies, as his chief of staff while the latter kept his corporate title during nearly three months in office (April 13 to July 10). The arrangement drew criticism from watchdog groups for creating an obvious conflict of interest, even though Senate ethics rules may not have prohibited it. Wilson held more than $20 million in company stock and continued selling shares worth about $450,000 while serving. Armstrong introduced a pipeline permitting bill that would benefit Williams, which cleared an initial vote. Ethics experts noted the appearance-of-conflict concern remains unresolved.
items.title: Senate Aide's Pipeline Company Ties Raise Ethics Questions

items.summary: On November 14, teenage batter Vaibhav Sooryavanshi became the youngest captain in men's T20 history at 15 years and 232 days. Leading Bihar to open the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy (SMAT) 2026-27 against Saurashtra at Holkar Stadium, Indore, he had won the toss and elected to bat first. The Bihar Cricket Association named a 17-member squad with Sooryavanshi captain for two matches; Suraj Kashyap was his deputy. He previously served as vice-captain of East Zone under Ishan Kishan in the Duleep Trophy, briefly leading when Kishan left due to injury.
items.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi Becomes Youngest Men's T20 Captain at 15

items.summary: Delhi Police allege a serving Indian Air Force wing commander traded classified military information to a Pakistani intelligence-linked operative in exchange for nude photographs, helping install spyware on five subordinates' devices. Contact ran 21 days (Jan 12–Apr 1, 2026). WhatsApp data shows 3,008 messages and 65 photos exchanged. Leaked details covered a secret drone unit, fighter deployments in Leh, and exercises at Mahajan Field Firing Range.
items.title: IAF Wing Commander Allegedly Traded War Plans for Nudes; Devices Spywared

items.summary: On Friday, the US National Weather Service (NWS) confirmed its radars were operating normally and that its radar website remained fully operational. The agency said outdated content from isolated webpages had been circulating online, but there was no actual radar outage. Previously, its website displayed reports of nationwide internet and communications problems that could have blocked access to products or shown stale information.
items.title: NWS Confirms Radars Operating Normally Amid Rumors of Outage
